adversarial_critique:
1. Scope & Eligibility Audit (`likely_ineligible_flag_e03_e04_e05_e07` / `moot_study_appears_ineligible`): Applying the exact 2026-10-13 / 2026-10-14 CK scope standard from A24/A26/A28—under which non-legal sociological exposures such as social trust (S1144) were excluded under E03 and upstream administrative approval outcomes such as building permits (S1121) were excluded under E04—S1140 fails both narrow Criterion 2 (E03) and Criterion 4 (E04) and should be flagged for PI removal from the 1,072-study corpus. First, on Criterion 2 (E03), all 125 applicant communities face the exact same RWSSP institutional and regulatory rules; the three focal hypotheses test informal, self-organized network/social capital metrics (count of external partner organizations contacted quarterly or more, two-step indirect reach to other communities, and copartner project-overlap cohesion, explicitly grounded in Granovetter 1973, Coleman 1988, Burt 1992/2000, and Putnam 2000). Although regulatory offices are among several possible contact types alongside banks, NGOs, and political parties, Shrestha explicitly notes on PDF p. 21 (journal p. 327) that the network tie count does not disaggregate regulatory exchanges from financial, technical, or partisan contacts, while formal RWSSP subsidy/ranking rules (% marginalized villagers eligible for a 50% cash-match subsidy, km distance to a bank for the 50% transport subsidy, expected time savings, and beneficiary count) enter solely as non-focal control variables. Second, on Criterion 4 (E04), as CK's own A29 ruling recognized, the binary dependent variable (1 = secured FY 2006/2007 RWSSP project funding, 0 = unfunded) captures competitive proposal approval at the end of the pre-construction planning phase—prior to the development, implementation, and post-implementation phases (PDF p. 5, p. 21)—and measures zero realized household or community water connection, service coverage, quality, continuity, or affordability.

2. Non-Fit Audit & Internal Database Inconsistency: Because S1140 appears scope-ineligible under E03 and E04, its SWiM family placement is substantively moot (`moot_study_appears_ineligible`). However, conditional on the PI retaining S1140 in the review, CK's A29 ruling moving the study out of Family B into `reasoned non-fit` would be fully justified: pooling pre-construction grant-application win probabilities with realized household water/sanitation access outcomes in Family B would conflate upstream grant-seeking network capital with actual last-mile service delivery. Notably, `effect_sizes.csv` retains an internal coding contradiction from before A29: `outcome_family` is still coded as `"service_coverage"` even though `exclusion_from_pooling_reason` explicitly states that the outcome is `"a community-level application outcome, not household connection, access or service quality"`.

3. Statistical Extraction Audit (`no_discrepancy_found`): While the headline Table 3 point estimate (`0.55***`), SE (`0.10`), cluster count (`37`), and predicted-probability sequences (`0.02 -> 0.38 -> 0.99`, `0.02 -> 0.044 -> 0.31`, and `0.43 -> 0.51 -> 0.86`) match the paper, `effect_sizes.csv` omits the numeric sample size `N = 125` (66 funded, 59 unfunded) from `sample_size` (storing only `"RWSSP applicant communities, Nepal"`), omits the Table 3 log-odds coefficients and SEs for the second and third focal exposures (`Indirect reach`: log odds `0.06**`, SE `0.03`; `Subgroup cohesion`: log odds `0.02**`, SE `0.01`), and inaccurately states in `comparator_definition` that covariates are held at their means for all comparisons when both the `0.02` 1-partner baseline and the entire `Indirect reach` probability sequence (`0.02`, `0.044`, `0.31`) hold `Number of partners = 1` (minimum) rather than its mean of `6.6` (rounded to `7` in text).

number_verification_detail:
Verified against Shrestha (2013, JPART 23:307-329; Advance Access May 10, 2012), Tables 1 and 3 (PDF pp. 11, 15-16; journal pp. 317, 321-322):
- Exact matches: Table 3 Full Model log odds for `Number of partners` = `0.55***` (`p < .01`), SE = `0.10`, Huber-White robust SEs (spelled `Hubert-White` in both paper and CSV) clustered across `37` UCINET hierarchical clusters (PDF p. 15 fn. 10). Predicted funding probabilities match text on PDF pp. 15-16: `Number of partners` rises from `0.02` (at 1 partner, 0 indirect reach) to `0.38` (at 7 partners; exact Table 1 mean is `6.6`, SD `3.16`, rounded to `7` by author on p. 15) to `0.99` (at 16 partners, max); `Indirect reach` rises from `0.02` (0 reach) to `0.044` (12, rounded from Table 1 mean `12.08`) to `0.31` (38, max); `Subgroup cohesion among partners` rises from `0.43` (0, min) to `0.51` (16, rounded from Table 1 mean `15.86`) to `0.86` (100, max). Qualitative note on remoteness matches Table 3 (`Remoteness of the community` log odds = `-0.08**`, SE = `0.04`, `p < .05`, rendered as `20.08**` due to PDF minus-sign glyph).
- Discrepancies / omissions in `effect_sizes.csv`: (1) `sample_size` stores only `"RWSSP applicant communities, Nepal"` and omits the exact numeric sample size `N = 125` (66 funded, 59 unfunded; printed on PDF pp. 4, 10, 11, and Table 3 p. 16 `N (number of cases) = 125`); (2) `effect_estimate` and `standard_error` report predicted probabilities for `Indirect reach` and `Subgroup cohesion` but omit their Table 3 log-odds point estimates and SEs (`Indirect reach`: log odds = `0.06**`, SE = `0.03`, `p < .05`; `Subgroup cohesion among partners`: log odds = `0.02**`, SE = `0.01`, `p < .05`); (3) `comparator_definition` states `"holding other covariates at their means"`, whereas PDF pp. 15-16 specify that the `0.02` probability for 1 partner holds `Indirect reach = 0` (minimum, not mean `12.08`) and the entire `Indirect reach` predicted-probability series (`0.02`, `0.044`, `0.31`) holds `Number of partners = 1` (minimum, isolated community, not mean `6.6`).
